Garden training develops into field harvesting, and a senior martial specialist pairs him with a noble female fighter for outside work. Their first mission brings them through starving bandits and into a fight against a dhol clan. Together they destroy the beasts threatening a local domain and recover herbs and demon materials. Over the following months, Wu Ying, Tou He, and the female martial specialist become an effective younger mission team. Wu Ying's cultivation stalls, but his body, bones, and martial integration improve. He completes Li Liu Tsong's introductory instruction, continues pill work and harvesting, and gives up blacksmithing for lack of time. Guidance from his father also helps him produce a short projected sword cut, a powerful but expensive step toward Dragon's Breath.

A senior gardener presses Wu Ying into a northern expedition seeking the final ingredient for a Core-stage bottleneck pill. Fairy Yang Fa Yuan explains that sponsorship and alliance create reciprocal duties, so Wu Ying accepts despite being below the usual cultivation requirement. Tou He volunteers to accompany him, Li Liu Tsong attends as an alchemical assistant, and Wu Ying acquires protective gear including a jade bracer able to release metal sword-qi. The expedition enters dangerous spirit lands, harvesting as it travels. A stalking beast kills one guard, and later battles with organized spirit beings cause further death and injury. The party escapes across a living earth bridge while poisonous cauldron smoke checks pursuit. Near the destination, a winged lion-like spirit beast accepts payment for passage, warns that the mountain is wrong, and finds something familiar in Wu Ying's full name without explaining why. At base camp, Li Liu Tsong challenges Wu Ying's broad resentment of nobles. Accepting his unfairness brings a brief enlightenment, raises him to Body Cleansing eleven, and leaves him intending to apologize to Yin Xue.

The expedition finds its scouts trapped behind a draining defensive formation by a peak Core demonic beast that has already killed several people. The rare flower is strategically vital because a rival sect has three pinnacle Core elders, so the survivors hold out until it blooms. Wu Ying helps maintain the formation, improves his aura suppression, and assists the expedition leader with the delicate harvest. The pill-refining elder produces five saint-level breakthrough pills. Two elders take pills immediately, and their cultivation draws so much ambient qi that the outer formation must be abandoned. The exhausted party makes a final stand. Tou He burns life force, Li Liu Tsong loses the use of a badly mangled arm, and Wu Ying's aura-masked sword attacks worsen the beast's wound but leave his sword broken and his lower legs torn. As the beast moves to kill him, one elder completes the breakthrough and intervenes. The advanced elder, expedition leader, and pill-refining elder destroy the beast. Wu Ying, Tou He, Li Liu Tsong, and the female martial specialist survive and return to Verdant Green Waters for treatment and rewards. Wu Ying remains at Body Cleansing eleven, now partly understanding that he seeks strength to preserve meaningful choices in a crisis.

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters swordsman at the Body Cleansing stage. His attempt to enter Energy Storage fails, and Elder Cheng tells him that greater insight and experience are needed as war approaches.
characters.name: Long Wu Ying

characters.description: Wu Ying's former-monk friend and fellow cultivator. He remains close to Wu Ying as war approaches and brings a companion's perspective to the discussion of whether sect cultivators owe service to the kingdom.
characters.name: Tou He

characters.description: A senior Verdant Green Waters cultivator who witnesses Wu Ying's unsuccessful breakthrough. She is an established adviser linked to Elder Cheng and offers guidance without taking control of Wu Ying's choices.
characters.name: Fairy Yang

characters.description: Wu Ying's master at Verdant Green Waters. He explains that Wu Ying's failed advance reflects a lack of insight rather than a simple shortage of qi, and he urges renewed practice as the prospect of war grows.
characters.name: Elder Cheng

characters.description: Wu Ying's noble girlfriend and a dedicated martial cultivator. She joins him and Tou He in discussing the approaching war and the sect's limited obligation to serve the kingdom.
characters.name: female martial specialist

characters.description: Wu Ying's mother. She supports his cultivation and urges him to keep more resources for his own progress, while cautioning him about his relationship with a noble cultivator.
characters.name: Wu Ying's mother

characters.description: Wu Ying's father. He supports his son's cultivation, encourages further study of the Long family sword style, and trusts Wu Ying to judge his own relationship.
characters.name: Wu Ying's father

characters.description: The library elder at Verdant Green Waters. He presents Wu Ying with three supplementary exercise options, cautions him to use his own judgment, and helps him choose a qi-regeneration practice.
characters.name: Elder Kuo

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters apothecarist senior and a former expedition companion of Wu Ying. She has arranged to enter the war with a prepared team and invites Wu Ying to join, though he declines.
characters.name: Liu Tsong

characters.description: A cultivator with a hostile history involving Wu Ying. Now at the beginning of Energy Storage, he warns that his father has stopped Wu Ying's village from relocating and provides useful information despite their past conflict.
characters.name: Yin Xue

characters.description: An archer and blacksmith recruited for Wu Ying's journey. The teammate agrees to accompany Wu Ying and Tou He in return for contribution points that Wu Ying will owe later.
characters.name: blacksmith teammate

characters.description: A branch noble of Wei holding rank in Shen, and Yin Xue's father. He makes the safety and departure of Wu Ying's village conditional on recovering his family's cultivation method from besieged Guetong.
characters.name: Lord Wen

characters.description: A Six Jade Gates patrol leader who stops Wu Ying and Tou He while they travel under assumed identities. He finds the sword display persuasive enough to dismiss suspicion and allow the pair onward.
characters.name: Tsui

characters.description: The Shen commander directing the siege of Guetong. He rejects the party's independent retrieval objective, detains its members when Wu Ying resists unconditional service, and forces them into the first assault wave.
characters.name: Lieutenant General Hao

characters.description: A metal-aspected Verdant Green Waters elder serving as the sect's representative with the Shen force. The elder warns Wu Ying that the commander wants firm military control over sect personnel and offers limited help during the party's detention.
characters.name: metal-aspected Verdant Green Waters elder

characters.description: The surviving member of a three-person White Tiger Sect contingent. After his two sworn brothers die in the assault on Guetong, he plans to use their death benefits to obtain a martial style, continue hunting demon beasts, and advance his cultivation.
characters.name: White Tiger Sect survivor

characters.description: A heavily armored enemy sword cultivator defending Guetong. He defeats two White Tiger Sect fighters on the battlements with a heavy blade and powerful sword intent, forcing Wu Ying's group to escape when the assault collapses.
characters.name: armored defending cultivator

recaps.ending: Wu Ying's party returns Lord Wen's authentic family cultivation method after escaping Guetong and surviving the journey out of enemy territory. Lord Wen keeps his oath, allowing Wu Ying's family and village to relocate under his protection, though the villagers resent the upheaval and the war remains unresolved. The blacksmith teammate survives severe wounds, while the final fates of Tsui and the armored defender are not established. Yin Xue has changed his qi route, advanced within Energy Storage, and retained an unexplained jade token from the mausoleum. Back at Verdant Green Waters, Wu Ying and the female martial specialist mutually end their romance, with any future friendship uncertain. Tou He returns safely, but his dantian problem remains open. After recovering and working to repay contribution points, Wu Ying understands that defining himself only by his peasant origins has constrained him. He accepts his ambition as a cultivator and opens his first Energy Storage meridian.
recaps.in_short: After failing to enter Energy Storage, Long Wu Ying tries to protect his village from the expanding war with Wei. Lord Wen agrees to let the villagers relocate only if Wu Ying's party retrieves the Wen family cultivation method from besieged Guetong. The Shen army detains the group and forces it into a costly assault, then abandons the siege without taking the city. Wu Ying and his companions infiltrate Guetong by river, recover the method from a family mausoleum, and escape after severe fighting. Lord Wen verifies the method and honors his oath, but the displaced villagers remain unhappy. Wu Ying's romance with the female martial specialist ends after their return. Having recognized that his attachment to a limited peasant identity caused his earlier blockage, Wu Ying finally enters Energy Storage, while war, family tension, Tou He's cultivation danger, Yin Xue's secrets, and Wu Ying's debts remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Long Wu Ying became a cultivator of Verdant Green Waters while retaining strong obligations to his family and village. Elder Cheng is his master, and the former monk Tou He is among his closest friends. His cultivation, friendships, and ties to his peasant origins shape his choices.

Wu Ying's attempt to enter Energy Storage fails because he lacks the necessary insight, not because he lacks qi. Elder Cheng advises experience and renewed training while war with Wei approaches. Military exercises teach Wu Ying that cultivators can change a battle but remain vulnerable without coordination. Letters from home reveal that his village may need to relocate, and Wu Ying prepares land near Verdant Green Waters while continuing herb work and a new qi-recovery exercise. He decides against volunteering for the war even after Liu Tsong joins the sect's expanded commitment. The danger becomes personal when Yin Xue warns that his father, the local lord, has blocked the village's departure. Fairy Yang recommends direct negotiation, and Tou He agrees to help. Wu Ying is now committed to protecting the villagers despite the political obstacle.

Wu Ying's party travels toward his home region as Tou He struggles with a dangerous exercise intended to enlarge his undersized dantian. At Lord Wen's estate, the group learns the price of the village's freedom. Lord Wen will permit and protect the relocation only if they recover his family's cultivation method from Guetong, a city already under siege. Wu Ying secures the promise by oath and accepts. The party crosses hostile territory in disguise, survives inspection by Tsui's Six Jade Gates patrol, and reaches the Shen army outside Guetong. Liu Tsong verifies their sect affiliation, but Lieutenant General Hao refuses to respect their separate mission. When Wu Ying will not submit without conditions, Hao detains the group and then assigns it to the first assault wave. The private effort to save a village has become compulsory front-line service, with no assurance that the party will ever reach the Wen family site.

The first assault on Guetong ends in retreat after heavy losses. An armored defender defeats two White Tiger Sect cultivators on the wall, and Wu Ying escapes with injuries. Their deaths are confirmed later by the surviving member of their group. During a later clash, Tou He leaves his post to aid endangered allies and Wu Ying follows. They arrive too late to save the Verdant Green Waters cultivators, though Tou He captures an enemy and Wu Ying recovers the fallen. The team is punished with supply-line duty, and Wu Ying's decision damages both his girlfriend's authority as team leader and their relationship. Wu Ying admits to himself that protecting Tou He, rather than a general rescue impulse, drove his disobedience. As the siege continues, Shen briefly gains sections of wall but cannot hold them. With a Wei reserve army approaching, Shen burns and bombards the area during withdrawal preparations and ambushes enemy cultivators who sortie after its engines. Guetong remains unconquered, and the cost of the campaign leaves Wu Ying increasingly troubled by the connection between military advantage and widespread loss.

Shen abandons the siege, but Wu Ying's group declines to remain with the withdrawing army because Lord Wen's bargain is still unfulfilled. After hiding near the river, the party attaches itself beneath an inbound ship and enters Guetong underwater. Inside the damaged city, Tou He pauses to comfort grieving civilians while the others reach the Wen family graveyard. Yin Xue gains entry, opens the mausoleum by blood, passes its protected test, and gives Wu Ying the cultivation-method tablets to settle a karmic debt. He separately keeps a jade token whose purpose remains unknown. Hostile relatives and city forces pursue the party. Wu Ying leads the retreat through the cemetery, and coordinated attacks break a ward blocking escape. At the wall, the injured blacksmith can barely continue and the armored cultivator traps the group. A noble ally's protective seal opens a route but rapidly drains its user, after which Tou He arrives with a herd of oxen and breaks the encirclement. The party reaches the wall with the method, but it is wounded, depleted, and still inside the enemy city's defenses.

Wu Ying coordinates the final escape from Guetong. Water released over the enemy is frozen into a barrier, Tou He incapacitates the armored pursuer, and the party descends outside the wall. After using an illusion formation to evade patrols, the group ambushes the force guarding its horses. Wu Ying critically wounds Tsui but loses both available swords and suffers serious injuries; Tsui's eventual fate is unknown. The companions recover their mounts and survive a difficult journey out of enemy territory, with the badly wounded blacksmith tied into the saddle. Lord Wen confirms that the recovered cultivation method is genuine and fulfills his oath by permitting Wu Ying's family and village to relocate under his protection. The move succeeds materially, but the villagers resent it, and Wu Ying recognizes that their expected life no longer fits him. At Verdant Green Waters, he and the female martial specialist agree that their romance is over. After weeks of recovery and herb work, Wu Ying understands that he failed earlier because he treated his peasant identity as a limit. Accepting his full ambition, he opens his first Energy Storage meridian. The war, family strain, Tou He's dantian weakness, Yin Xue's jade token, and Wu Ying's contribution-point debts remain open.

characters.description: A returning Verdant Green Waters elder, swordsman, and leader of the wandering gatherers. His cultivation joins the sword to the Seven Winds body art, while his position binds him to students, sect duties, and the search for rare spiritual resources.
characters.name: Wu Ying

characters.description: Wu Ying's close companion, a wood cultivator and formation theorist with extensive trading connections. Her practical judgment and independent outlook complement his wandering path, while her commercial network reaches beyond the sect.
characters.name: Wood cultivator

characters.description: A former monk, Verdant Green Waters elder, and fire-staff cultivator. He is a trusted friend of Wu Ying and a formidable practitioner of flame techniques.
characters.name: Tou He

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters elder and Wu Ying's martial sister. Fairy Yang moves between sect affairs, intelligence work, and direct cultivation matters with a firm concern for discipline.
characters.name: Fairy Yang

characters.description: Verdant Green Waters' leading apothecarist and a longstanding ally of Wu Ying. She is a trusted source of medical and alchemical expertise whose work supports both individual cultivators and the sect's wider advancement.
characters.name: Liu Tsong

characters.description: The Nascent Soul leader of Verdant Green Waters, responsible for its cultivators, political standing, and long-term survival. The sect head balances formidable personal power with the demands of administration and succession.
characters.name: Sect head

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters official responsible for intelligence and foreign affairs. The guardian approaches Wu Ying during his training to discuss a diplomatic mission involving Wei and Tsui.
characters.name: Right guardian

characters.description: A returning Shen nobleman and cultivator who has integrated a demonic replacement eye and arm. He joins the embassy at Wei's request while facing unresolved family, political, and cultivation obligations.
characters.name: Yin Xue

characters.description: A Core Formation prince whom Wu Ying once rescued and offended. He accepts an expensive pill as reparation without abandoning his hostility, and his place in the royal delegation makes Wu Ying partly responsible for his security.
characters.name: Fourth prince of Shen

characters.description: A disguised attacker who targets the fourth prince with poison during Wei's reception. The assassin conceals their cultivation, sacrifices an arm to escape Wu Ying, and uses a specialized dagger to breach a forming containment ward.
characters.name: Assassin

characters.description: A young royal of Wei who cultivates water with notable promise. Her planned union with Shen's fourth prince supports the alliance, although court expectations may narrow her future advancement.
characters.name: Second princess of Wei

characters.description: A Nascent Soul cultivator who secretly guards Wei's king. Her Tao was shaped by grief surrounding her husband's betrayal and death.
characters.name: Weeping Widow

characters.description: Three surviving Wei swordsmen from a tradition known for mediation and defensive swordwork. Each has attained the heart of the sword, and one asks to test swords with Wu Ying after noticing his weapon.
characters.name: Iron Pass sword cultivators

characters.description: Wei's first prince is initially assessed as a pill-supported cultivator of limited martial importance. He remains part of the royal and political landscape surrounding the new alliance and the approaching talks with Tsui.
characters.name: First prince of Wei

characters.description: A senior Shen representative carrying the kingdom's political burdens at the Tsui talks. He must manage an unexpectedly altered balance of powerful cultivators and makes hard choices about the fourth prince's continued presence.
characters.name: First prince of Shen

characters.description: A feared Nascent Soul field commander announced as part of Tsui's unusually powerful negotiating party. Reports portray the general as formidable, though the delegation has not yet confirmed the stories about their methods.
characters.name: Tsui guerrilla general

characters.description: An aged formation cultivator travelling with Verdant Green Waters. Despite infirmity and a cultivation base strained by age, he accompanies the delegation to the border negotiations.
characters.name: Six Flags Patriarch

characters.description: Tsui's king and the central power behind its delegation. He arrives with a compact, disciplined vanguard and projects a dominating aura strong enough to require several allied Nascent Soul cultivators to answer him.
characters.name: Ruler of Tsui

characters.description: An allied patriarch skilled in formations and writing-based cultivation. He detects covert illusion workings around the negotiations, quietly disrupts them, and advises Wu Ying about the martial challenges being arranged.
characters.name: Eight Stanzas patriarch

recaps.ending: The ruler of Tsui is overwhelmed when Wu Ying forces his consuming Dao to take in the collapsing world spirit ring and Fairy Yang cuts away the unequal karmic bonds supporting him. The disaster reshapes the border and becomes a sealed gateway to a new, hazardous mystical realm. Only fragments of the ruler are recovered, leaving a measure of uncertainty about his complete destruction, while the damaged Tsui fortress retreats. Wu Ying is alive but absent, with his immortal body, soul integration, core, and link to the ring catastrophically damaged. His wood-cultivator companion remains his committed partner and final rescuer. The sect head survives his wounds, and Fairy Yang becomes temporary right guardian. Only one Iron Pass swordsman survives, permanently injured, and joins Verdant Green Waters as a visiting elder to preserve his tradition. Wei's first prince is reported dead, the first prince of Shen is apparently lost, and regional succession and alliances remain unsettled. Yin Xue survives without his demonic arm and eye, but his meridians are failing. He secretly possesses the ruler's second demonic heart and must choose between death and a transformation that threatens his humanity and future rebirths. The assassins' sponsor also remains unknown.
recaps.in_short: Wu Ying survives the reconstruction of his body, but his soul remains imperfectly joined to it. He joins a Verdant Green Waters embassy seeking to unite Shen and Wei and avert Tsui's drought-driven war. An assassination attempt, divided Wei loyalties, and Tsui's coercive cultivation system expose the talks as a trap. Wei's first prince sides with Tsui, and the ruler of Tsui proves to be a half-immortal sustained by demonic power and his army's linked strength. Wu Ying sacrifices a clean ascension to summon tribulation, then destroys his world spirit ring inside the ruler's consuming Dao. Fairy Yang severs the ruler's unjust karmic support, and the resulting collapse defeats him while remaking the border into a sealed mystical realm. Wu Ying survives but disappears in grave condition. Tsui withdraws, Wei's succession is unstable, and Verdant Green Waters suffers heavy losses. Yin Xue secretly keeps the ruler's second demonic heart, which may save his ruined meridians only by transforming him into a demon.

recaps.text: Previously: Wu Ying rose from a farming background to become the Verdant Gatherer, a Verdant Green Waters elder and the head of its wandering gatherers. His path joined sword cultivation to the Seven Winds body art and brought him close to immortality, but advancement left difficult work ahead. He carries Zhen, possesses a vast world spirit ring, and has accumulated obligations to his sect, students, friends, and homeland. Tou He remains his trusted companion in cultivation, while Liu Tsong supports him through medicine and alchemy. Fairy Yang is his martial sister and an increasingly important political organizer. Wu Ying's closest bond is with a wood cultivator and formation theorist whose mercantile network gives her influence beyond the sect. Yin Xue follows a dangerous path involving a demonic replacement eye and arm, and his history with Wu Ying remains strained. Wu Ying enters this volume with powerful allies and exceptional resources, but also with responsibilities that make every step toward immortality consequential for those around him.

Wu Ying completes a hazardous reconstruction after the phoenix heart powering the ritual runs short. The sect head delays the tribulation long enough for him to reform, and Wu Ying survives the lightning with an immortal wind body. Recovery reveals striking new abilities: he can dissolve into wind, sense nearby space through moving air, and evade almost by instinct. Those reflexes are powerful but not yet fully under conscious control. A supervised spar with Tou He demonstrates Wu Ying's greater speed and strength, then escalates beyond either man's intent. Wu Ying's ordinary spirit sword shatters against Tou He's defense, and fragments carrying sword intent wound Tou He badly enough to leave his aura damaged, though he is expected to recover. The accident reinforces how dangerous Wu Ying's strength has become. He also learns that his advancement is incomplete. His compressed core needs years of reinforcement, and soul and body must still be merged before a final ascension attempt. During his recovery, Wu Ying and his wood-cultivator companion commit themselves to a shared future as Tao companions, while accepting that formal arrangements and the dangers of cultivation still lie ahead.

Wu Ying begins testing his abilities in the sect's hidden mystic realm, where destructive techniques can be used without endangering the wider sect. His developing fifth Wandering Dragon form still cannot break a Tao-infused monolith, and access to the realm is limited by its long recovery time. At the same time, the sect head insists that Wu Ying train a credible replacement for the Department of Wandering Gatherers before ascending. No single student appears able to assume all of his duties, even if a pending Core Formation attempt succeeds. An external crisis overtakes these concerns. Drought and regional weakness are pushing Tsui toward expansion, while Shen seeks a stronger alliance with Wei. Verdant Green Waters asks Wu Ying and his companion to join an armed embassy intended both to negotiate and to deter aggression. Wu Ying resists exposing them to Tsui's assassins and destabilizing tactics, but accepts because refusing could leave many people vulnerable to war. Tou He remains behind. Yin Xue joins at Wei's request despite unresolved disputes over his demonic replacements and family cultivation matters. After prolonged arrangements over passage, authority, and security, the embassy departs in a concealed flying pagoda.

The embassy reaches drought-stricken Wei after the Shen royal party joins it. Wu Ying gives the fourth prince an expensive pill as reparation for an earlier offense, but their relationship remains tense. At Wei's floating palace, Wu Ying detects a poisoned assassin disguised as a servant and prevents the fourth prince's murder. The attacker severs an arm, breaches a forming ward, and escapes, leaving the sponsor unknown. Suspects include Tsui, factions within Shen or Wei, demonic interests, and rival sects. Wei accelerates its alliance with Shen. The fourth prince marries Wei's second princess, though the political match may constrain her cultivation. Wu Ying also meets three surviving Iron Pass sword cultivators and loses a restricted spar after exceeding its agreed speed. The exchange exposes weaknesses in his inherited sword forms and gives him valuable instruction. The apparent alliance remains unstable. Wei unexpectedly adds two Nascent Soul cultivators to the Tsui delegation, while Tsui announces that its king, royal-guard commander, and guerrilla general will attend. Shen keeps the newly married fourth prince with the mission and plans a costly spiritual contract to secure any peace. The talks now carry enough concentrated power to become a major battle if diplomacy fails.

The delegations establish a fortified meeting ground on the remote Wei-Tsui border. Wu Ying quietly warns a nearby hidden settlement that the gathered armies may discover it, providing concealment talismans without assuming control of the residents' choices. The negotiation site takes a week to complete because every formation is repeatedly inspected. During the delay, Yin Xue asks Wu Ying to challenge Wei's demand that he spend ten years training one of its families. Wu Ying promises only to raise the matter. Wu Ying's own condition also worsens. A conversation that reduces him to a weapon destabilizes his sense of self, and the sect head explains that his rapid bodily advancement has left soul and body dangerously out of step. When Tsui approaches the talks, nearly thirty apparent soldiers reveal themselves as Core Formation survivors of a bound vanguard. Their ruler arrives with several figures of possible Nascent Soul strength and tests the assembly with a dominating aura. Gift exchanges then expose Tsui's strategy. Food and civilian aid are answered with martial equipment designed to provoke disputes between Shen and Wei. A captured cultivation method shows how Tsui links weaker practitioners to stronger ones, accelerating growth while creating impurity and dependence. Yin Xue also detects demonic chi in the delegation and concludes that the king combines orthodox and demonic power while sustaining his followers through his own soul.

Substantive talks stall over borders, reparations, enforcement, and the spiritual cost of binding rulers to an agreement. Wu Ying remains the fourth prince's guard while observing the delegations and gathering military intelligence. In arranged sparring, Yin Xue defeats a Tsui colonel, and Wu Ying defeats three more vanguard cultivators without showing his full strength. He learns that their compatible auras let nearby soldiers reinforce a fighter, then proves that a sufficiently refined cutting intent can sever that support. The weakness is useful but difficult to exploit against the entire unit. Informal diplomacy reveals that Wei is divided among isolationists, supporters of peace, and a faction willing to side with Tsui against Shen. Wu Ying also protects fleeing villagers from a provisioning hunt through misdirection and a warning, though he cannot guarantee their safety. At a feast, the Tsui ruler forces Wu Ying to accept a politically charged gift, prompting Wei and Shen to answer with gifts of their own and worsening the first Shen prince's hostility. The three offerings are more symbolic than immediately useful. In private, the ruler declares that he intends not merely regional conquest but eventual defiance of heaven, blaming celestial inaction for mortal suffering. Wu Ying shares some criticism of that inaction but rejects the ruler's proposed rebellion.

Four masked assassins attempt to place a destructive spatial formation against the Verdant Green Waters pagoda. Wu Ying interrupts them and pursues the same armless attacker who targeted the fourth prince. The assassin uses decoys, trapped talismans, poison, and a malformed duplicate before deliberately self-destructing. All four attackers die rather than be captured, and their sponsor remains unidentified. Tsui then forces the talks to resume. During treaty disputes, Wei's first prince reveals a secret alliance with Tsui that sacrifices his father and country in exchange for food and a redirection of Tsui's armies. The negotiating party is already surrounded. Yin Xue appears to consider Tsui's offer of survival, but when combat begins he fights for Shen beside the Iron Pass swordsmen. Wu Ying attacks the ruler directly and discovers that ordinary Nascent Soul strength cannot overcome him. The ruler's war Tao suppresses Wu Ying's wind and threatens the retreating princes. Wu Ying's wood-cultivator companion activates the pagoda's prepared formation, turning Tsui's shared cultivation links against its forces. The Eight Stanzas patriarch adds writing-based attacks that damage the vanguard's foundations. Their combined work strips away the ruler's army-linked reinforcement, leaving him isolated but still powerful enough to require a decisive finishing attack.

The ruler's equipment and true strength reveal him as a half-immortal approaching ascension. With no ordinary means left to stop him, Wu Ying breaks open his own core and begins an emergency ascension, calling heavenly tribulation to the battlefield. His soul and body start to merge, but he rejects the heavenly wind's demand for obedience and understands that the attempt cannot end cleanly. He returns to battle anyway, accepting the loss of his own ascent to protect his companions, sect, and homeland. The resulting power lets him keep the ruler within the tribulation's reach. Lightning passes through Wu Ying and their locked weapons, injuring both men, while the ruler's artifacts absorb part of the punishment. When the ruler tries to flee, Wu Ying pursues, and the ruler's own dominance Tao makes retreat difficult. Elsewhere, the severing of Tsui's shared support gives Shen and Wei loyalists an advantage. Wu Ying's companion recognizes that he cannot win alone. Rather than duel the Tsui guerrilla general directly, she uses a spatial pendant to imprison the general, freeing allied power for the main struggle. Wu Ying is critically failing under the incomplete ascension, while the ruler remains alive as the tribulation approaches its climax.

The last tribulation strike leaves Wu Ying unconscious and nearly destroyed, yet the ruler survives, heals with an exceptional pill, wounds the Verdant Green Waters sect head through an expendable subordinate, and kills an allied patriarch. His concealed demonic Dao begins consuming the battlefield. Wu Ying wakes with his body and soul separating, refuses an escape that would abandon the remaining defenders, and asks his allies to carry him close enough for one final attempt. Yin Xue sacrifices his demonic arm and eye to interrupt the ruler's power. Fairy Yang guides the assault with her Dao of balance, while the sect head and other survivors spend their strength to create seconds of opportunity. Wu Ying's Karma Severing Cut fails, but a diversion by his companion lets him take back his true world spirit ring and throw it into the ruler's consuming Dao. The ring contains a continent-sized world. The ruler cannot reject it without contradicting his own Dao, yet consuming it tears apart the unstable union of immortal body, demonic core, and limitless hunger. As the ring collapses, the ruler consumes his remaining followers and destroys the reciprocal basis of his authority. Fairy Yang severs those unequal karmic bonds, and the backlash overwhelms him. The border erupts in spatial and elemental devastation. Wu Ying loses consciousness, and his companion uses a final gift to keep him alive, while the ruler's precise fate and the disaster's full extent remain unresolved at chapter's end.

characters.description: A returning Verdant Green Waters cultivator whose sword skill and wind-shaped body have reached Core Formation. He arrives badly injured and has difficulty preserving a human perspective when heavenly wind exerts its influence.
characters.name: Wu Ying

characters.description: Wu Ying's traveling companion, a wood cultivator who fights with enchanted fans. She recognizes when heavenly wind is drawing him away from human concerns and intervenes, then faces a hostile reception as his guest at Verdant Green Waters.
characters.name: Wood cultivator

characters.description: A hostile Verdant Green Waters official who once tormented Wu Ying as a junior. He attacks Wu Ying's companion at the mountain entrance, invokes stricter security rules, and makes the returning travelers continue without his assistance.
characters.name: Gate guardian

characters.description: A returning companion of Wu Ying and an elder of Verdant Green Waters. The former monk arrives at the gate with two of Wu Ying's allies, once again wearing the robes of sect authority as the dispute over admission continues.
characters.name: Tou He

characters.description: Wu Ying's elder martial sister and an influential member of Verdant Green Waters. She welcomes his traveling companion as family, uses her authority to grant the visitor honored status, and explains the formal trial awaiting Wu Ying.
characters.name: Fa Yuan

characters.description: An apothecary and ally who examines Wu Ying soon after his return. She finds damage throughout his body, including badly distorted meridians, and makes clear that ordinary medicinal baths cannot provide a complete recovery.
characters.name: Liu Tsong

characters.description: Wu Ying's elderly parents are mortal farmers in his home village. They take pride in his pursuit of immortality and welcome his Tao companion into the family.
characters.name: Wu Ying's parents

characters.description: The Nascent Soul leader of Verdant Green Waters, presiding over the assembled elders at Wu Ying's judgment. He listens as Wu Ying defends his conduct and authorizes a combat test when the returning cultivator asks the sect to measure his blade.
characters.name: Sect head

characters.description: The metal-aspected head of the outer sect and a spear-wielding elder. He is selected to test Wu Ying before the gathered leadership after Wu Ying turns his suitability hearing into a public demonstration of strength.
characters.name: Elder Mo

characters.description: An earth-aspected Verdant Green Waters elder who specializes in grappling. He enters the arena to test Wu Ying, yields when Wu Ying brings a sword to bear, and remains for the ordered three-against-one fight.
characters.name: Martial elder

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters cultivator present among the elders judging Wu Ying. His visible replacements include an eye and a hand, marking the physical cost of experiences that preceded the returning cultivator's public hearing.
characters.name: Yin Xue

characters.description: The name by which Wu Ying's elder martial sister is now known. She stands with him during his confrontation with the sect leadership, even while criticizing the risks he takes, and remains one of his clearest political allies.
characters.name: Fairy Yang

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters elder recruited after serving as successor to a smaller, failing sect. His domain centers on collection, and at his introduction he seeks a cooperative relationship with Wu Ying.
characters.name: Senior gathering elder

characters.description: A trusted authority over the sect library. Wu Ying asks him to judge a collection of cultivation manuals, techniques, and gathering works for possible acquisition, while Elder Kuo weighs usefulness against unsafe duplication.
characters.name: Elder Kuo

characters.description: A peak Energy Storage gatherer whose failed Core Formation attempt cracked the core that was taking shape. Though another attempt may be possible after many years, he now trains aspirants overlooked by the established gathering program.
characters.name: Former gathering senior

characters.description: An aging Verdant Green Waters elder who has surrendered his guardian post as an old injury worsens. Believing he lingered too long in the comforts of service, he plans a final, probably fatal attempt to reach Nascent Soul and asks Wu Ying to witness it.
characters.name: Former guardian

characters.description: The sect's medical authority who assesses Wu Ying alongside Liu Tsong. The physician identifies his injuries as damage to his control over his transformed body and warns that treatment may offer only a partial repair without further enlightenment.
characters.name: Sect physician

characters.description: The only Body Cleansing cultivator to survive the early stages of Wu Ying's entry trial. His control is exceptional enough to keep his aura contained even while unconscious, although doing so leaves him physically weaker than a mortal during the test.
characters.name: Body-cleansing student

characters.description: One of the two students who currently meet Wu Ying's standards in the new Department of Wandering Gatherers. Gui Ting stands out while the shrinking class receives individualized training in herbs, aura perception, martial ability, and field survival.
characters.name: Gui Ting

characters.description: One of the two strongest remaining students in Wu Ying's new department. Xia Hui has endured its demanding mix of gathering study, aura control, and martial training while several less committed or less capable classmates have departed.
characters.name: Xia Hui

characters.description: The Verdant Green Waters official responsible for foreign affairs and an extensive intelligence network. He approaches Wu Ying with paid work that would turn knowledge from exile and overseas relationships into useful contacts for the sect.
characters.name: Right guardian

characters.description: A wandering-gatherer trainee whose drive for rapid advancement outweighs Wu Ying's warnings about safety. After surviving a dangerous plant during the field examination, the trainee refuses advice to slow down and accept more time in the outer sect.
characters.name: Ambitious trainee

characters.description: The first-ranked graduate of the Department of Wandering Gatherers' initial field examination. Wu Ying appoints this unnamed trainee as the department's senior disciple and offers help toward a future Core Formation breakthrough.
characters.name: Senior disciple

recaps.ending: Several years after returning, Wu Ying remains at Verdant Green Waters as an established elder and head of a growing Department of Wandering Gatherers. Its first students now undertake supervised and independent fieldwork, and the political attempt to abolish it has failed. The rival gathering elder has lost influence and some control over valuable herbs. Wu Ying's medicinal baths have improved his condition without curing it, and strenuous travel can still trigger a relapse. His wood-cultivator partner continues to travel, gather with him when possible, and seek materials for his treatment. During enforced recovery, Wu Ying creates the Old Dragon form, a fourth sword form built around restrained motion and holding a position under pressure. He also settles on a coherent understanding of the Seven Winds, joining five earthly winds with heavenly authority and the corrective force of the thousand hells, though further advancement remains uncertain. Tou He is still sealed away attempting to rebuild his immortal soul. Fairy Yang's network continues exposing exploitation and tracking dark-sect remnants, while war and displacement worsen beyond the sect.
recaps.in_short: Wu Ying returns injured to Verdant Green Waters and survives a hostile judgment that ends with him leading a new Department of Wandering Gatherers. The unfunded school becomes both his obligation and his means of serving the sect while experimental baths slowly repair his unstable wind body. He recruits and tests a first class, confronts political opposition, and begins intelligence work as Tou He struggles against a heaven-driven purifying flame. The students complete a dangerous wilderness examination, but Tou He then seals himself away to reconstruct his immortal soul and an aging former guardian dies attempting Nascent Soul ascension. A later effort to dissolve Wu Ying's department fails, and the rival gathering elder loses influence. Over several years the department expands, Wu Ying develops the defensive Old Dragon sword form, and his bond with the traveling wood cultivator endures. He remains only partly healed, ending with a clearer understanding of the Seven Winds as regional instability grows.

recaps.text: Previously: Wu Ying left Verdant Green Waters after being banished for striking a prince, but continued to act as a loyal representative of the sect during his travels. He helped free kidnapped prodigies, exposed a dark sect's ties to demonic forces, and gathered foreign herbs, pills, manuals, and cultivation knowledge. His journeys also carried him far from his mortal parents and the mountain where he first trained. By the time he turns homeward, he has reached Core Formation as a sword-wielding wind cultivator and is known as the Verdant Gatherer. Tou He, an established Verdant Green Waters elder, former monk, and fire-staff cultivator, remains one of Wu Ying's returning companions. Wu Ying therefore approaches his old sect with a record of service and valuable resources, but his banishment and long absence leave his standing uncertain.

Wu Ying and his wood-cultivator companion return to Verdant Green Waters, but heavenly wind still threatens his human perspective and his body remains badly damaged. A hostile gate guardian attacks the visitor, then sect officials delay their entry as a calculated insult. Tou He, Fa Yuan, and Liu Tsong eventually arrive. Fa Yuan grants the visitor honored guest status, while Liu Tsong determines that Wu Ying's distorted meridians and injured organs will require prolonged treatment. Wu Ying visits his aging parents and introduces his companion as his Tao companion. Inside the sect, he sees both the damage from an earlier attack and the rebuilding that followed. Fa Yuan warns that established elders regard his strength, reputation, and possible promotion as a threat. At the formal hearing, the gate guardian presents Wu Ying as disobedient and dangerous. Wu Ying answers by citing his service and the knowledge and resources brought home, then demands that the elders test his ability rather than judge him by submission. The sect head accepts the challenge and sends Elder Mo into the arena.

Wu Ying defeats Elder Mo and an earth-aspected martial elder, then controls a three-against-one fight by turning rain, wind, and a prepared storm against his opponents. The sect head ends Wu Ying's tornado and judges him powerful enough to approach Nascent Soul strength, but also difficult for the sect to control. Wu Ying refuses to deny his grievances or surrender his independence. Instead of expelling him, the sect head makes him head of a new Department of Wandering Gatherers. The appointment carries elder standing but little comfort: Wu Ying must produce three peak Energy Storage gatherers within a decade, including one with a route toward Core Formation, and receives no initial funding. Yin Xue offers money but admits his loyalty remains tied to the gate guardian. Wu Ying begins raising resources by offering acquired texts to Elder Kuo, while withholding his personal sword inheritance. His inspection of the established gathering operation exposes the need for his department. Its senior elder has improved profitable herb production but favors trainees with gifts and leaves other aspirants poorly taught. A former gathering senior, injured during a failed Core Formation attempt, has been training those neglected candidates.

An aging former guardian tells Wu Ying that attachment to a comfortable role stalled his cultivation, and asks Wu Ying to witness a likely fatal attempt at Nascent Soul ascension. Meanwhile, creating the new department proves expensive and logistically difficult. Wu Ying needs suitable land, equipment, travel permissions, and emergency protections for students. Liu Tsong confirms that his transformed body remains unstable and may require years of treatment or a final insight into the Seven Winds. His wood-cultivator companion faces challenges from sect elders, criticizes how his work has consumed his attention, and helps him reconnect with his parents. Advice from his father gives Wu Ying a teaching principle: provide a fair opportunity, then concentrate effort on adults who persist. Wu Ying announces open trials. Tou He, still troubled by the destructive behavior of his altered flame, enters closed-door cultivation. More than two dozen applicants arrive, but Wu Ying tests control and judgment rather than cultivation rank. He requires mortal-level aura suppression, applies pressure, leads the candidates through difficult terrain, and arranges a supervised beast ambush. Eight remain, including three female gatherers, a senior gatherer, three students linked to the established program, and one exceptionally controlled Body Cleansing cultivator.

Wu Ying continues the practical examination by testing identification, harvesting skill, restraint, and ecological judgment. The strongest applicants demonstrate that valuable resources are not always safe or wise to harvest immediately. He retains most of the finalists despite suspecting that two may report to the senior gathering elder, reasoning that his earliest lessons contain little worth stealing. His deeper physical damage remains untouched by surface cleansing, and proposed remedies range from slow alchemical restructuring to much more dangerous elemental destruction and renewal. The sect head grants the department permission to work beyond the mountain and gives Wu Ying access to the elders' library, while making clear that better support must be earned through service. The gate guardian then explains the basis of his hostility: he believes Wu Ying has diverted talented friends from their proper destinies and calls him a calamity. The accusation unsettles Wu Ying. His companion points to those friends' accomplishments and insists that their choices remain their own. Fairy Yang agrees that people inevitably affect one another's karma, but rejects the claim that Wu Ying has uniquely ruined those around him. Wu Ying accepts the slower alchemical treatment plan and emerges less willing to deny his friends' agency.

Wu Ying finances his obligations by lecturing, although the established gathering leadership restricts his access to profitable inner-sect classes. A demanding core-area class broadens his own knowledge while forcing him to improve his teaching. In the department, only Gui Ting and Xia Hui consistently meet his standards. Liu Tsong and the sect physician begin an experimental medicinal-bath regimen that clears some damaged channels but leaves Wu Ying depleted. Recovery will require repeated treatments over years and a continuing supply of rare materials. Rival gatherers harass his students while he rests, but the class refuses to escalate the dispute. Wu Ying's traveling partner prepares to leave again, using her merchant network to seek treatment resources and contacts. He continues limited sword practice, unable to complete a fourth form because his Tao lacks the necessary resolution. The sect's right guardian then offers paid intelligence work based on Wu Ying's foreign relationships, giving the department another possible source of contribution points. Tou He returns from seclusion with an injured arm and reveals the central danger of his altered flame: it carries a heavenly imperative to purge what heaven rejects. He intends to resist that command until he controls the flame rather than obeying it.

Months of teaching, intelligence correspondence, and punishing medicinal baths pass. The department's Body Cleansing student advances surprisingly far in the outer-sect tournament through endurance and an unpleasant but legal defensive tactic, provoking Elder Mo and other opponents to challenge the department's legitimacy. Yin Xue warns that the political hostility reflects a senior leader's preferred vision for Verdant Green Waters. Wu Ying answers the pressure by sending his remaining students on a month-long wilderness examination. They must gather valuable herbs, return to camp each night, manage dangerous wildlife, and prove they can make independent decisions. Gui Ting and Xia Hui compete separately for first-disciple standing, while other students rely on complementary teamwork. The trainees ultimately choose to confront a group of Xing Tian. Their baited formation does not work as planned, but they defeat a coordinated counterattack with injuries. Back at the sect, Wu Ying lets market valuation and negotiation form part of the final assessment. He appoints an unnamed senior disciple, conditionally offers another student a subordinate rank, passes three only as a team, and dismisses an impatient trainee who ignored repeated safety advice. At the same time, Tou He enters a sealed formation to reconstruct his immortal soul and seek freedom from the harmful Tao anchor controlling his flame.

The former guardian attempts the leap from Core Formation to Nascent Soul. Protective preparations and a pill cannot save him when heavenly lightning overwhelms the process after his core shatters, killing him before the nascent soul can be born. Fairy Yang helps Wu Ying understand the attempt as the culmination of a life centered on guardianship and sacrifice. Wu Ying in turn recognizes teaching as a path that can strengthen both his own understanding and the sect. The trainee dismissed after the field examination remains resentful and secretly uses unrevoked travel privileges to gather alone. That administrative lapse becomes ammunition when Wu Ying is summoned before the sect leadership. Opponents first accuse him of building a loyal subsect, then shift toward charges of incompetence and waste. Liu Tsong and Fairy Yang defend the individualized training, and Wu Ying admits and corrects the mistake concerning the former trainee. The rival gathering elder asks that the department be dissolved and Wu Ying placed under his supervision. By winter, the answer is evident: the department survives and its students increasingly work in teams or independently. Its rival loses influence and control over valuable herbs. Wu Ying continues treatment with supplies sent by his traveling partner, while Tou He remains sealed in soul reconstruction and the new senior disciple begins an independent search for breakthrough ingredients.

Over the following years, demand for trained wandering gatherers increases and Wu Ying's department expands. He adds written and contribution-point requirements for applicants, while senior students take on more fieldwork and some teaching. The first senior disciple repeatedly seeks rare ingredients needed for advancement, despite pill impurities that may obstruct later cultivation. Wu Ying obtains limited supervised entry to territory controlled by a Nascent Soul spirit beast, extending the department's access to valuable wilderness. His own recovery remains incomplete. A long expedition with his wood-cultivator partner causes his old injuries to flare again, and she later departs in search of more treatment resources. Forced to limit his movement, Wu Ying develops the Old Dragon form, a fourth sword form designed to hold ground with economical motion while injured or outnumbered. Fairy Yang's network of female cultivators grows into a means of sharing information, exposing exploitation, and pursuing dark-sect infiltrators connected to their master's loss. Tou He remains sealed away attempting to remake his immortal soul. Wu Ying finally clarifies his Seven Winds: five belong to the earthly world, heavenly wind imposes authority, and the thousand hells provide judgment, penance, and renewal. He remains at Verdant Green Waters as an injured teacher and department head while war and displacement worsen beyond the sect.

characters.description: An Energy Storage cultivator of Verdant Green Waters who studies swordsmanship and herb gathering under Elder Cheng. Debts and obligations have slowed his progress, but he commits himself to finding three rare materials after his master returns gravely poisoned.
characters.name: Wu Ying

characters.description: Wu Ying's former-monk friend and a staff fighter of Verdant Green Waters. He helps with sect assignments, supports the planned cure expedition, and continues searching for a safe treatment for his damaged and unusually small dantian.
characters.name: Tou He

characters.description: Wu Ying's master and an elder of Verdant Green Waters. He returns from a secret mission weakened by Three Seasons poison, a lethal condition whose cure requires a sun lotus, a Chan Chu heart, and a Ben spirit stone.
characters.name: Elder Cheng

characters.description: Elder Cheng's other disciple and Wu Ying's martial sister. She escaped the mission that poisoned their master and organizes the research, route planning, recruitment, and practical preparations for the cure expedition.
characters.name: Fa Yuan

characters.description: A senior apothecarist of Verdant Green Waters and Wu Ying's private teacher. She explains that the required saint-class medicine exceeds what she can reliably produce in the field, and the war prevents her from leaving the sect's medical work.
characters.name: Liu Tsong

characters.description: A hook-sword fighter and former wandering cultivator who has joined Verdant Green Waters. He spars with Wu Ying after Wu Ying's recent breakthrough and says he sought the sect's protection because the approaching troubles are too large to escape alone.
characters.name: Former wandering cultivator

characters.description: The expedition's specialist pill maker. He is capable but arrogant, shows contempt toward mortals, and pursues the party's musician too directly until Wu Ying and Tou He confront him about his conduct.
characters.name: Expedition apothecary

characters.description: A musician recruited for the cure expedition. Her presence draws unwanted attention from the apothecary.
characters.name: Expedition musician

characters.description: A former friend of Wu Ying who advanced to second-stage Energy Storage through military service. He has since been reassigned to the city as a city-guard lieutenant, with time there to continue cultivating.
characters.name: City-guard lieutenant

characters.description: The official hosting the cultivator auction city. He receives Fa Yuan on sect business, handles valuable items submitted for sale, and asks her to advise his water-aspected daughter, whose limited interest in cultivation worries him.
characters.name: Magistrate

characters.description: A young water-aspected cultivator with enough talent to benefit from Fa Yuan's instruction. Her father asks the visiting cultivator to advise her because, despite her aptitude, she shows little desire to make cultivation her path.
characters.name: Magistrate's daughter

characters.description: A visiting cultivator who assaults a restaurant hostess during the crowded auction period. Wu Ying turns the confrontation into a formal public challenge to keep the dispute from becoming a broader fight.
characters.name: Visiting sect cultivator

characters.description: A trident-wielding direct disciple sent against an already wounded Wu Ying in the public succession challenge. Fresh and well prepared, he presses his attack beyond the point expected in a sparring match.
characters.name: Opposing direct disciple

characters.description: The Grey Heavens Auction House official who conducts the cultivation sale under a strict prohibition on violence. Wu Ying cannot read his aura and estimates that his cultivation is at least high Core Formation.
characters.name: Auction hallmaster

characters.description: An elder of Heavenly Lake whose party is already hostile toward the Verdant Green Waters delegation. He watches them openly at the auction, competes for valuable cultivation materials, and presents an immediate concern for Fa Yuan's party.
characters.name: Heavenly Lake sect elder

characters.description: An inner disciple of Heavenly Lake who approaches Fa Yuan after his elder outbids her for a stone needed in Elder Cheng's cure. He invites her to discuss the stone at the sect's residence that night, creating a possible route to the missing material.
characters.name: Heavenly Lake inner disciple

characters.description: A city officer handling the aftermath of the Heavenly Lake conflict. He presents a strict public position while privately promising to protect Fa Yuan in custody and keep watch over the detained opposition.
characters.name: City guard captain

characters.description: The expedition's musician, now identified by name during the final Chan Chu hunt. She uses air-chi guzheng music to interfere with the metal-aspected beast's aura, movements, and meridians while the other fighters seek an opening.
characters.name: Wang Min

characters.description: A swordsman of concealed cultivation leading armed fighters who hold the expedition apothecary hostage. He demands the cure materials, appears stronger than Wu Ying, and uses the prisoner's injuries and explosive talismans as leverage.
characters.name: Dark-sect swordsman leader

recaps.ending: Wu Ying survives a sword thrust through his chest because Wang Min and the injured apothecary recover enough cure material to prepare a powerful medicinal bath. The treatment repairs his severe wounds and strengthens his body, though it does not advance his cultivation stage. Fa Yuan rejoins him after the authorities accept enough evidence to release her. Her tracking mark on the stolen Ben spirit stone leads the sect to a merchant connected with its sale, but the wider dark-sect organization remains unexposed. The surviving expedition members are sent toward sect support, and a sun lotus continues growing inside Wu Ying's living world spirit ring. Elder Cheng receives the antidote and rapidly recovers. He assumes responsibility for the expedition's debts and begins training Wu Ying more intensely for the trouble ahead. Tou He remains alive but may have meridian damage, while the apothecary's poisoned and badly damaged hand tendons still require treatment. Fa Yuan briefs the sect's senior leadership, and the broader Shen-Wei destabilization remains open.
recaps.in_short: Elder Cheng returns to Verdant Green Waters with a lethal poison, prompting Wu Ying, Fa Yuan, Tou He, and a small expedition to seek three rare cure materials. Their journey tests the group against spirit beasts, hostile cultivators, and a conspiracy using corrupted chi and sacrifice-based cultivation. After Fa Yuan kills a Heavenly Lake elder and is detained, Wu Ying leads the remaining party to secure sun lotus and a powerful Chan Chu heart. Enemy cultivators capture and torture the apothecary, steal key materials, and nearly kill Wu Ying. Wang Min and the apothecary save him with a lotus blossom, a Chan Chu heart, and costly medicines, while Fa Yuan's tracking mark provides a lead to the stolen stone. Elder Cheng receives the antidote and recovers. Wu Ying returns to harsher training with a strengthened body and a new sword, while the dark-sect network, Tou He's cultivation damage, and the apothecary's injured hands remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Wu Ying is a disciple of Verdant Green Waters, trained in swordsmanship and herb gathering under Elder Cheng. His advancement through Energy Storage is constrained by debts and obligations to his family and village. Tou He, his former-monk friend, has joined the inner sect but still seeks a safe answer to his damaged dantian. Elder Cheng returns from a dangerous mission suffering from Three Seasons poison, which will kill him within months. Fa Yuan, Cheng's other disciple, believes the poisoning is connected to a dark sect encouraging conflict between Shen and Wei. The cure requires a sun lotus blossom, a powerful Chan Chu heart, and a Ben spirit stone. Liu Tsong cannot reliably make the saint-class medicine in the field, so Wu Ying and Fa Yuan begin planning an expedition, researching locations, preservation, and recruitment while Cheng's condition worsens.

So far this book: Wu Ying embraces a demanding routine of cultivation, sword practice, movement training, gathering study, and expedition research. His rejection of the dark sect's cruel path brings an enlightenment and another open meridian, though the beasts required for the cure remain beyond his present strength. The group still lacks a dependable field apothecarist, a route covering all three ingredients, and a storage method that can preserve a fresh Chan Chu heart. Elder Cheng discovers the preparations and initially objects to his disciples risking themselves for him. He ultimately accepts that they must follow their own path, arranges formal sect backing and equipment payment, and acknowledges Tou He's offer to join. War needs prevent the sect from assigning more elders, leaving Fa Yuan to lead an under-resourced expedition whose remaining members must be recruited quickly.

Wu Ying opens a third meridian and learns an active aura defense and a scent-based method for detecting chi. Fa Yuan recruits a compact party consisting of Wu Ying, Tou He, a former wandering cultivator, an apothecary, and a musician. Their river journey is interrupted by water tigers, but the musician weakens the beasts with chi-infused music while the others defend the vessel. Forced onto an overland route, the group enters a marsh in search of the needed amphibian. Spirit fish wound Tou He and shock the musician before the party reaches a yellow-bile frog. A core-stage snake seizes Fa Yuan during the fight, leaving Wu Ying and the others to finish the frog while she battles the larger threat alone. They kill both creatures and collect valuable materials, but the frog is not the Chan Chu needed for Elder Cheng's antidote. The failed hunt nonetheless proves that the expedition can cooperate under pressure.

After recovering from the marsh, the expedition reaches the auction city. Wu Ying deepens his understanding of cutting and sword intent, while the former wandering cultivator advances and the musician receives an enlightenment. Wu Ying reunites with a former friend serving in the city guard, then challenges a visiting cultivator who assaulted a hostess and defeats him publicly. The resulting spectacle grows into a succession contest between sect and wandering cultivators. Tou He wins six consecutive bouts before his small dantian leaves him depleted. Wu Ying then fights through a series of opponents while injured and exhausted. In his sixth bout, a trident user continues attacking after Wu Ying is effectively beaten. Wu Ying creates a weaponless chi strike shaped by his new insight into sharpness and stops the assault. Fa Yuan prevents the opponent's master from retaliating. The attacker's burnt, rotten-smelling chi matches a wrongness Wu Ying previously sensed around a suspected elder, turning the rumored dark-sect threat into a concrete lead.

At the cultivation auction, the hostile Heavenly Lake elder buys a stone needed for Elder Cheng's cure after outbidding Fa Yuan. Wu Ying spends most of his funds on a depleted living world spirit ring, choosing a long-term gathering resource over a better sword. A Heavenly Lake disciple invites Fa Yuan to negotiate for the cure stone. Wu Ying warns the expedition that their opponents' distorted chi may connect them to the attack on Elder Cheng. While Fa Yuan meets the elder, Wu Ying's companions disobey her instruction to remain inside and watch the Heavenly Lake residence with detection talismans. The disciple and several fighters attack them, while Fa Yuan battles the elder separately. She later explains that he demanded her lifeblood for a practice that consumes cultivation potential to create temporary power. She refused and killed him. Although officials find some support for her allegations, she remains detained pending investigation. Fa Yuan gives the recovered cure stone to Wu Ying and orders him to continue. Wu Ying becomes expedition leader and leaves to find the sun lotus and adequate Chan Chu heart without her.

Wu Ying leads the expedition away from the city while using talismans, waterways, and off-road travel to hide its route. He transplants an immature sun lotus into his living world spirit ring, then guides the group to a secluded valley containing mature plants. A core-stage spirit carp guards the lake. The musician calms it while Wu Ying swims out under concealment, harvests two blossoms into ice-jade boxes, and removes a complete plant for his ring. The carp breaks free of the musical influence and injures him, but Tou He pulls him ashore. With both a sun lotus and the previously recovered spirit stone secured, Wu Ying sends the apothecary toward sect support carrying those ingredients. Wu Ying, Tou He, the musician, and the former wandering cultivator continue to a marsh for the last requirement. Tou He reaches five open meridians during the hard journey. The reduced party kills several dangerous beasts and takes a three-legged frog heart, but it is too small for the intended cure, leaving the central hunt unfinished.

As the party prepares to leave the marsh, it finds a Core Formation Chan Chu and risks one final ambush. The metal-aspected beast resists their initial trap and wounds the fighters with explosive spikes of chi. Tou He's fire attacks exploit its elemental weakness, while Wang Min's guzheng music gradually disrupts its aura, muscles, and meridians. Wu Ying and the former wandering cultivator concentrate on an injured leg until Wang Min briefly locks the creature's meridians. They open a fatal wound, although Wu Ying's sword and Wang Min's treasured guzheng are destroyed. The group promptly harvests and preserves the heart. Everyone is injured and depleted, and Tou He fears damage to his meridians, but the expedition now holds a suitable replacement heart. They leave the marsh, avoid a protected flock of Ben, report success to Verdant Green Waters, and head toward a city where they expect rapid passage home.

Near the city, Wu Ying's party encounters armed cultivators holding the expedition apothecary captive. His hands have been broken, and the captors demand the materials he had been carrying. Wu Ying surrenders the sun lotus to secure his release, only to discover explosive metal-chi talismans fixed across the prisoner's body. Wang Min estimates that their controller must remain nearby, so she rides away with the apothecary and tries to take him beyond activation range. The enemy leader claims the expedition's accusations lack proof and suggests that Wu Ying and Fa Yuan have been used to draw hidden opponents into the open. Wu Ying recognizes that the cure quest may have served as bait. He displays the remaining Chan Chu heart and begins another exchange, then turns the handover into a signal to attack. Wang Min covertly freezes the fighters' chi with her music, allowing Wu Ying to wound several enemies, but the stronger swordsman drives a blade through Wu Ying's chest. He falls unconscious while Tou He and the former wandering cultivator are also badly injured.

Wu Ying awakens in a medicinal cauldron after Wang Min and the apothecary use a recovered sun lotus blossom, a Chan Chu heart, and costly herbs to save him. By cultivating with the Yellow Emperor's methods during the treatment, he repairs the damage to his chest and lung and emerges physically stronger, though without advancing his cultivation stage. Fa Yuan rejoins him after the authorities accept enough of her evidence to release her. She has sent the surviving companions and Wu Ying's world spirit ring toward sect aid. A lotus remains alive inside the ring. Fa Yuan also marked the stolen Ben spirit stone before the expedition, allowing the sect to trace it to a merchant and continue the investigation. Back at Verdant Green Waters, Elder Cheng has received the antidote and recovered rapidly. He assumes responsibility for repaying the expedition members and seeks treatment for the apothecary's ruined hand tendons. Fa Yuan reports to the sect's senior leadership, while Elder Cheng gives Wu Ying a harsher training regimen for the coming danger. The expedition succeeds, but the larger dark-sect conspiracy remains unresolved.

characters.description: A Verdant Green Waters disciple, herb gatherer, swordsman, and student of Elder Cheng. An awakened bloodline has made him stronger but altered his meridians and acupoints, leaving ordinary cultivation dangerous while he searches for a method his body can survive.
characters.name: Wu Ying

characters.description: Wu Ying's former-monk friend and a fire-staff cultivator. Damage to his lower dantian has resisted treatment, forcing him to consider the risky prospect of opening another dantian and greatly lengthening his path through Energy Storage.
characters.name: Tou He

characters.description: Wu Ying's master at Verdant Green Waters and his instructor in the jian. He supervises Wu Ying's recovery, forbids unsafe advancement, and helps seek a cultivation method compatible with his student's transformed body.
characters.name: Elder Cheng

characters.description: The Verdant Green Waters apothecarist who teaches and treats Wu Ying. He identifies the newly active bloodline behind Wu Ying's survival and warns that medicine cannot by itself resolve the resulting damage and cultivation constraints.
characters.name: Liu Tsong

characters.description: Wu Ying's elder martial sister and Elder Cheng's other disciple. She helps fund Wu Ying's care, regards that support as a family duty, and hosts cultural instruction for members of Verdant Green Waters.
characters.name: Fairy Yang

characters.description: The library elder of Verdant Green Waters. He assists the search for rare cultivation texts and recognizes that Wu Ying's unusual spirit ring warrants access to costly reference works.
characters.name: Elder Kuo

characters.description: A cultivator who remains friendly with Wu Ying after their romantic relationship has ended. She discusses the increase in banditry and possible Dark Sect involvement with him.
characters.name: Wu Ying's former partner

characters.description: Wu Ying's teacher in gathering and the care of spiritual resources. She identifies his ring as a genuine growing world spirit ring, warns that knowledge of it could provoke violence, and asks him to surrender it without explaining why.
characters.name: Wu Ying's gathering teacher

characters.description: An older cultivator at peak Energy Storage who joins Wu Ying's mixed group for the journey to the specialist sect.
characters.name: The older escort

characters.description: Wu Ying and Tou He's travelling companion on the journey to the specialist sect. An experienced gatherer, he fights with a bow and hooked swords.
characters.name: The former wandering cultivator

characters.description: A spear-wielding noblewoman travelling with Wu Ying's party to the specialist sect. She is reluctant to cooperate with the others but fights beside them when demon beasts attack during the journey.
characters.name: The noblewoman

characters.description: The visitors-hall elder at the island sect that specializes in unusual constitutions. He receives the party from Verdant Green Waters and arranges lodging and guidance for its members.
characters.name: Elder Huang

characters.description: A senior cultivator at the host sect with an earlier connection to Tou He's temple. He accepts the group's concern about a possible Dark Sect presence, promises discreet observation, and supplies talismans for communication and emergencies.
characters.name: The honorary monk elder

characters.description: A visiting cultivator seeking treatment for damage caused by products sold as legitimate cultivation elixirs. She explains that the aids concealed their own dependence, accepts that Wu Ying attacked her without malicious intent, and expects later recompense.
characters.name: The former cultivation-aid user

characters.description: Two brothers from the host sect who join the crane-hunting expedition. They are water cultivators equipped with spears and talismans, adding defensive strength to the mixed group assembled by Wu Ying's companions.
characters.name: The host-sect brothers

characters.description: A visiting cultivator whose group draws suspicion because of its connection to people harmed by corrupt cultivation aids. Wu Ying determines that she does not carry the distinctive taint, making her a possible lead rather than a proven enemy.
characters.name: The Whistling Iron Monkey cultivator

characters.description: A poisoned and wounded elder defending the upper library after its formations are breached. Even in that condition, the elder remains the central defender against a hostile Core cultivator attacking the tower.
characters.name: The library formation elder

recaps.ending:
The attack on the host sect fails, but the tower and library suffer extensive damage and many defenders are lost. Wu Ying, Tou He, their former wandering companion, the Whistling Iron Monkey allies, and the library defenders hold long enough for the wounded formation elder to destroy a hostile Core cultivator's core. Two other enemy Core cultivators also die, as does one protector of the host sect. The noblewoman escapes amid fires in the tower, and the Dark Sect's wider network and internal collaborators remain unresolved.

Wu Ying spends almost two months healing. Five Winds Body has restored much of his condition and strengthened his bones and joints, but the exact nature of his dragon ancestry, his long-term health, and the soul method suited to him remain unsettled. Elder Huang rewards his warning and service with a personal copy of Seven Winds Body under a binding secrecy oath. Wu Ying leaves the sect with the former wandering cultivator and seeks a middle course between reckless intervention and ignoring harm. Tou He stays behind for a time to refill and stabilize his enlarged cultivation capacity and to assist reconstruction. Wu Ying's next challenge is reconciling Seven Winds with his bloodline while changing his soul cultivation path.
recaps.in_short: An awakened dragon bloodline has transformed Wu Ying's body but filled it with dangerous, self-renewing chi. He travels with Tou He and a former wandering cultivator to a sect that studies unusual constitutions, where he is told he may have only a year to live. While earning access to cultivation manuals, he uncovers victims of addictive Dark Sect aids and signs of an active conspiracy. Tou He successfully opens a second dantian, but Wu Ying nearly exhausts himself supporting the breakthrough. Wu Ying finally understands that Five Winds Body must balance his altered chi instead of removing it, restoring his strength in time to resist a coordinated assault on the host sect. The defenders repel the attack at severe cost, though the noblewoman and other conspirators escape. After nearly two months of healing, Wu Ying receives Seven Winds Body and leaves with his former wandering companion, while Tou He remains temporarily to recover and help rebuild.

recaps.text:
Previously: Wu Ying returned to Verdant Green Waters carrying the consequences of an unplanned medicinal bath. A previously hidden, apparently nonhuman bloodline allowed him to survive, but it altered his body and made further cultivation unsafe. Liu Tsong can treat the damage but cannot identify a compatible long-term method, while Elder Cheng orders Wu Ying to stop opening meridians until the danger is understood. Wu Ying remains committed to cultivation despite the risk.

Tou He faces a separate crisis: damage to his lower dantian may require him to open another dantian and rebuild much of his Energy Storage progress. Wu Ying also learns that his world spirit ring is a genuine growing space whose value must remain secret. His gathering teacher warns him about the danger, while Elder Kuo helps him research it. With ordinary wood cultivation worsening Wu Ying's condition and no adequate manual at Verdant Green Waters, both friends need expertise beyond their home sect.

So far: Ordinary cleansing cannot remove the blockages spreading through Wu Ying's altered body. A test of wood cultivation ends in collapse, and the dark marks associated with his condition continue to grow. During a challenge at the training grounds, however, a wooden practice jian produces an extraordinary response. Wu Ying's chi moves through it with unusual ease, his sword intent breaks through the protective barrier, and the weapon shatters. His body then heals rapidly enough to expel embedded splinters, though the effort drains his dantian.

The episode shows that Wu Ying's condition is not merely a simple elemental affinity. It offers unusual strength, healing, and a close bond with wooden weapons, but it also triggers destructive reactions he cannot yet control.
